claims.text: Interviewer reports whether the field team was proactively contacted by community or party representatives, not whether the respondent holds partisan views.

evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Records the interviewer's own felt threat during this interview, an interviewer-side experience distinct from physical threat or respondent attitude.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Separates reported physical threat during the interview from the broader felt-threat item, so a felt danger need not involve bodily threat.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Interviewer's judgment of respondent candor, an attributed demeanor assessed by the fieldworker rather than a verified truthfulness measure.
Forced choice between presidential exemption from law and courts versus obligatory obedience, capturing asserted view rather than observed executive conduct.

evidence.quote: The [president] must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: Elicits stance on military intervention in politics generally, a general principle rather than a judgment about any specific coup or event.

evidence.quote: armed forces should never intervene in the country's political process

claims.text: Asks who ought to hold oversight responsibility for elected MPs, a normative allocation question rather than a report of actual oversight practice.

evidence.quote: Who should be responsible for: making sure that, once elected

claims.text: Parallel normative allocation for holding the president accountable, permitting comparison of expected overseers across two offices.
Hypothetical likelihood judgment about community harassment of a woman candidate, a belief about possible futures rather than a report of observed harassment.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed by others in the community?

claims.text: Respondent evaluates the desired direction and amount of government action on women's rights, a judgment about appropriate state effort.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more than they are doing now

claims.text: Single-choice priority among listed women's-rights issues, producing a ranking constrained by the offered option set rather than independent importance.

evidence.quote: which of the following issues related to women's rights and equality

claims.text: Conditional justification judgment about emergency policing of health mandates, an endorsement of a possible measure rather than a report of enforcement.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Respondent's belief about who commissioned the survey, a perception of sponsorship that need not match the actual implementing organization.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Consent-like willingness to be recontacted for follow-up, with a not-applicable category for respondents lacking a mobile number.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

holds.missing: Interviewer-administered items but no field identifying which interviewer or interviewer attributes; Q111/Q112/Q113 appear only in the locator, not the supplied packet.
holds.why: Cannot attribute observed demeanour or threat reports to specific interviewers or test interviewer effects within this packet.

holds.missing: No country/wave field in the supplied selected items to verify which constitution, president, or armed forces the bracketed placeholders resolve to.
holds.why: Target referent of the abstract institutional wording cannot be fixed from the cited fields alone.

holds.missing: No routing evidence showing whether Q51A and Q51B were asked of all respondents and whether Q51B was conditioned on any prior answer.
holds.why: Cannot establish whether the priority item reflects an unconditioned choice or a routed subsample.
